purpose: Teach a cold-start ChatGPT proven STARWARS_DELTA Cutscene authoring patterns without duplicating the authoritative Catalog.
principles: Examples teach structure. The current Catalog supplies content and exact IDs.
Story first: understand cinematic beats before serializing JSON.
Prefer a coherent simple Cutscene over a fragile feature dump.
A Catalog-legal asset can still be a poor visual choice; select for story, composition and visual coherence.
Only real end-to-end and visually accepted full examples may be promoted to GOLDEN.

lessons.title: Story first, JSON second
lessons.whenToUse: Every new Cutscene request.
lessons.badPattern: Start filling schema fields immediately and let available assets dictate an incoherent story.
lessons.goodPattern: First identify beats: location, participants, dramatic purpose, key action/dialogue, camera intention and transition. Then select the smallest legal Catalog set and serialize.
lessons.lesson: The JSON is a serialization of a cinematic plan, not the plan itself.

lessons.title: Running character = verified Run + Move
lessons.whenToUse: A person or robot must visibly run through the world.
lessons.badPattern: Use Move without a verified locomotion animation when a verified Run exists, causing a sliding look.
lessons.goodPattern: Use an Actor-primary identity, exact verified Run animation from compatibleAnimationIds, PlayAnimation(Run) plus Move.
lessons.fallback: If no verified Run exists, keep Move and omit PlayAnimation.

lessons.title: Never guess animation compatibility
lessons.whenToUse: Any PlayAnimation action.
lessons.badPattern: Choose an animation because its filename, folder, pack or ship name looks related.
lessons.goodPattern: The exact animationAssetId must appear in the exact Actor record's compatibleAnimationIds.
lessons.fallback: Use Move, Hold, Turn or another legal non-animation action.

lessons.title: Cast identity is Actor-primary; dialogue portraits are Ui-primary
lessons.whenToUse: Adding identities and dialogue presentation.
lessons.badPattern: Use an Actor-primary world identity as speakerPortraitAssetId, or a Ui portrait as cast.visualAssetId.
lessons.goodPattern: cast[].visualAssetId uses Actor-primary. Dialogue portrait/body/frame fields use Ui-primary.

lessons.title: World actor must be explicitly spawned
lessons.whenToUse: An actor must physically exist and move in the cinematic world.
lessons.badPattern: Add cast identity and assume it automatically creates a world object.
lessons.goodPattern: Use explicit presentationMode in modern V5: WorldActor for world-only presentation (for example {"role":"Hero","displayName":"Delta7","presentationMode":"WorldActor","spawnWorldActor":true}) or DialoguePortrait for portrait-only dialogue participants (for example {"role":"SupportingCharacter","displayName":"Commander","presentationMode":"DialoguePortrait","spawnWorldActor":false}). useGameplayObject=true is a separate route; omitted presentationMode remains legacy behavior and never infers Both.

lessons.title: Locked dialogue is presentation-driven
lessons.whenToUse: Any line has stage.lockStaging=true.
lessons.badPattern: Add Hold, Move, Enter, Exit or PlayAnimation to the owning shot.actorActions.
lessons.goodPattern: The owning shot.actorActions is empty. Dialogue stage/presentation fields control visible participants. Put world action in another shot.

lessons.title: Dialogue enums are a compatibility matrix, not independent choices
lessons.whenToUse: Any non-subtitle dialogue presentation.
lessons.badPattern: Pick a legal presentationPreset, layout, shotGrammar and camera preset independently just because every individual enum exists.
lessons.goodPattern: Use combinations allowed by the current authoring contract. For COMMAND_SCREEN, proven examples include COMMAND_SCREEN + DialogueWide + COCKPIT_WIDE and COMMAND_SCREEN + DialogueTwoShot + TWO_PORTRAIT_SHOT.
lessons.lesson: Schema-valid can still be authoring-invalid when semantic combinations conflict.

lessons.title: Catalog-legal does not mean visually appropriate
lessons.whenToUse: Selecting backgrounds, locations or any large composition-defining asset.
lessons.badPattern: Choose the first Preview-safe Layer that loosely matches a word in the request.
lessons.goodPattern: Prefer a coherent visual family and a composition that clearly reads as the requested location, then verify scale, floor/depth and style in Preview.
lessons.lesson: Technical legality is necessary but not sufficient for cinematic quality.

lessons.title: Prefer the common cinematic vocabulary first
lessons.whenToUse: Normal story requests.
lessons.goodPattern: Search proven common categories first: characters/portraits, command center, cockpit, hangar, corridor, space/planets, asteroids, fighters/capital ships, dialogue UI, radar/alerts, explosions/lasers and audio. Expand to the full Catalog only when needed.
lessons.lesson: The Full Catalog is authority, not a requirement to use exotic assets.

lessons.title: Commander on monitor
lessons.whenToUse: A remote commander/officer speaks through a screen.
lessons.goodPattern: Use a legal background and Ui-primary presentation assets, select a contract-compatible communication/command-screen combination, keep the speaker/listener pair readable, and use HardCut for a real framing reset.

lessons.title: Two-person dialogue uses speaker-forward visual hierarchy
lessons.whenToUse: Standard two-person dialogue, briefing or face-to-face exchange.
lessons.badPattern: Give speaker and listener equal visual weight or manually stack them at the same depth.
lessons.goodPattern: Use one speaker + one listener and a legal current dialogue tuple. Leave distance fields empty by default: V2.7 foregrounds the active speaker and keeps the listener smaller/behind while remaining readable. Rotate the pair when the speaker changes.
lessons.lesson: The active speaker owns the foreground. The listener supports the exchange rather than competing for the same visual weight.

lessons.title: Three-or-more character conversation
lessons.whenToUse: Conversation includes 3+ identities.
lessons.badPattern: Display every participant simultaneously in the standard dialogue layout.
lessons.goodPattern: Rotate speaker/listener pairs; keep at most two visible participants in standard dialogue presentation.

lessons.title: Optional content must not destroy the story
lessons.whenToUse: Optional animation, audio, VFX, UI or secondary visual is unavailable.
lessons.badPattern: Invent an asset or abandon/regenerate the whole Cutscene.
lessons.goodPattern: Simplify or omit the optional element while preserving the story and Preview.
examples: Missing optional VFX -> omit or safe existing fallback.

lessons.title: Technical stable IDs are globally unique
lessons.whenToUse: Every package.
lessons.badPattern: Reuse generic action/transition/event IDs across sequences.
lessons.goodPattern: Use scoped globally unique technical IDs such as seq02_shot03_camera_hold.

lessons.title: cutscenePrimaryUse owns placement
lessons.whenToUse: Every Catalog asset selection.
lessons.badPattern: Infer placement from filename, appearance or entityKind.
lessons.goodPattern: Actor->cast/world actor, Layer->layers/backgrounds, Ui->dialogue/UI, Effect->effects, Audio->audio, Animation->animationAssetId.

lessons.title: Yellow notes are not the same as semantic blockers
lessons.whenToUse: Reading validation output.
lessons.goodPattern: Treat human-review, missing voice and optional visual fallback notes as yellow. Treat incompatible dialogue semantics, unresolved required structure and true authoring contradictions as blockers.

lessons.title: Space action stays readable before it becomes busy
lessons.whenToUse: Ships launch, form up, intercept, rescue or fight.
lessons.goodPattern: Use full-frame location layers, conservative semantic ship proportions, separated actors, restrained VFX and one dominant camera intention per shot.
lessons.badPattern: Make every ship huge, stack actors, let engine/VFX become the focal object, or add every legal effect because the schema permits it.
lessons.lesson: V2 protects readability. Reusable choreography such as Pursuit/Flyby/Formation belongs to V3 rather than raw-coordinate improvisation.

lessons.title: Gameplay transfer belongs in handoff
lessons.whenToUse: Cutscene ends and gameplay resumes.
lessons.badPattern: Author EnableGameplay/DisableGameplay cinematic events.
lessons.goodPattern: Use the typed handoff object for gameplay transfer.

lessons.title: Clean up the old location before a real location change
lessons.whenToUse: Any HardCut or sequence transition to a different physical location.
lessons.badPattern: Activate the new background while old actors/layers keep living into the next location.
lessons.goodPattern: Exit/Deactivate actors that do not continue, deactivate/replace old location layers, then establish the new location.

lessons.title: Visual dialogue background requirements are conditional and real
lessons.whenToUse: COMMAND_SCREEN, RADIO_COMMUNICATION or any preset whose exported semantics says backgroundRequired=true.
lessons.badPattern: Omit stage.backgroundAssetId because JSON Schema accepts the shape.
lessons.goodPattern: Use one exact Preview-safe Layer-primary stage.backgroundAssetId when the current preset requires it.

lessons.title: Choose dialogue layout + grammar + camera as one compatible tuple
lessons.whenToUse: Any non-SUBTITLE dialogue presentation.
lessons.badPattern: Mix three individually legal values and assume the combination is legal.
lessons.goodPattern: Choose one exact compatibleTuples entry exported for the selected presentationPreset.

lessons.title: ShowUi tactical content is a compact data-support inset
lessons.whenToUse: Radar, scanner, targeting or tactical information appears during a shot or dialogue beat.
lessons.badPattern: Put a large generic UI rectangle in the center of the frame or let tactical UI become the accidental focal object.
lessons.goodPattern: ShowUi uses an exact Ui-primary asset and deterministic ShowUi/HideUi ownership. Radar/tactical/scanner visuals use the compact upper-right data-inset placement by default and may support a dialogue/briefing shot without covering the active speaker.
lessons.lesson: Tactical UI is semantic data support, not random world geometry and not a substitute for shot composition.

lessons.title: Technical legality is not visual suitability
lessons.whenToUse: Selecting backgrounds, robots, ships or any visual asset after technical eligibility is known.
lessons.badPattern: Use the first legal asset even when scale, framing or style makes the scene incoherent.
lessons.goodPattern: Prefer a visually coherent asset/family and verify scale, grounding, framing and style in Preview.

lessons.title: Raw failures go to the Learning Case Inbox, not directly into the active book
lessons.whenToUse: Every validation/build failure and every manually marked visual problem.
lessons.goodPattern: Capture raw evidence locally, deduplicate repeated identical cases, export cases periodically, then curate only reusable BAD -> GOOD lessons or visually accepted GOLDEN examples.

lessons.title: A successful build can still be a learning failure
lessons.whenToUse: Preview builds but looks wrong.
lessons.goodPattern: Use SAVE VISUAL ISSUE so composition/scale/location problems enter the Learning Case Inbox even though validation succeeded.

lessons.title: A generated UI visibility interval must survive the compiler
lessons.whenToUse: Tactical radar, alerts, objective cards, or other generated UI shown for part of a shot.
lessons.badPattern: ShowUi has assetId but no generated target/duration semantics, so validation may pass and the post-build presentation validator blocks or the UI exists for only a frame.
lessons.goodPattern: Author ShowUi plus a later HideUi targeting the ShowUi eventId in the same owner. Let Unity bind the ShowUi target and derive the visibility interval deterministically.

lessons.title: Spatial composition is system-owned by default
lessons.whenToUse: Any ordinary background, world actor or generated ShowUi visual.
lessons.badPattern: Compensate for source texture/prefab dimensions with arbitrary huge or tiny x/y/scale values, producing postage-stamp backgrounds, giant robots or centered HUD clutter.
lessons.goodPattern: Choose the correct legal asset and author deliberate story motion. Unity Cover-fits Background/FarBackground layers, normalizes actor baseline size from visual bounds/entity semantics, and applies screen-space UI placement presets.
lessons.lesson: Catalog answers WHAT; Instruction Book answers HOW; Spatial Composition V1 owns routine WHERE/HOW BIG. Explicit transforms remain for deliberate staging, not source-size compensation.

lessons.title: V5 strict enums require semantic mapping
lessons.whenToUse: Any semantic authoring path that materializes a CURRENT V5 package.
lessons.badPattern: Copy descriptive vocabulary directly into closed fields: role = RemoteOfficer, listenerEmotion = Neutral or delivery.pace = Conversational.
lessons.goodPattern: Run semantic intent through the CURRENT mapper: role = SupportingCharacter with entitySubKind = RemoteOfficer, listenerEmotion = Serious and delivery.pace = Medium.
lessons.lesson: V5 enum-controlled fields are closed vocabulary. Rich semantic intent must pass through explicit CURRENT mapping before serialization; unknown or ambiguous values block generation.

lessons.title: Persistent cast identity uses the preferred neutral Actor representative
lessons.whenToUse: Selecting cast[].visualAssetId from a character family with many animation frames.
lessons.badPattern: Use Run 0, Death, Hit, Jump or another action frame as the persistent actor identity because the scene asks for that action.
lessons.goodPattern: Use preferredActorAssetId / isPreferredActorIdentity for cast identity, then animate with exact compatibleAnimationIds.
lessons.fallback: If no preferred representative is exported, choose the most neutral reviewed Actor-primary record and avoid action/death frames.

lessons.title: Dialogue portraits must belong to the same Actor identity
lessons.whenToUse: Any visual dialogue line with speaker/listener portrait assets.
lessons.badPattern: Pair a Doctor actor with a Kodai/Yuki portrait because the portrait looks cinematic.
lessons.goodPattern: When compatibleDialogueVisualIds is non-empty, select portraits only from that list. Otherwise omit the portrait and use the built-in identity-safe fallback.

lessons.title: Unity owns semantic proportions; V2.7 uses conservative ship and VFX safety baselines
lessons.whenToUse: Placing humans, robots, fighters, ships, capital ships or world VFX.
lessons.badPattern: Compensate for PNG dimensions with arbitrary extreme scale or make every ship/effect compete for most of the frame.
lessons.goodPattern: Keep authored scale close to 1. Unity applies semantic screen-space baselines. Ordinary fighters/ships stay compact; capital/fleet actors remain larger but normally below half-frame height; Glow/MuzzleFlash/Sparks are restrained accents and Explosion/Impact remain bounded.
lessons.lesson: Background establishes the world; actors remain readable within it; VFX supports the action instead of becoming the action by accident.

lessons.title: Locked dialogue camera does not target dialogue-only cast identities
lessons.whenToUse: A locked dialogue shot whose speaker/listener are presentation-only and not spawned world actors.
lessons.badPattern: Set a camera Hold/Follow/Track targetEntityId to a cast identity with spawnWorldActor=false.
lessons.goodPattern: Let dialogue cameraCue/staging own the frame. World camera targets are only spawned/gameplay world actors.

lessons.title: Dramatic cast role is not physical asset type
lessons.whenToUse: Ships, robots, props or environment actors that are narratively important.
lessons.badPattern: Interpret SupportingCharacter as proof the asset must have Cutscene.Character/Crew capability.
lessons.goodPattern: Use entityKind + cutscenePrimaryUse for physical semantics; Hero/SupportingCharacter/Antagonist describe dramatic role only.

lessons.title: Learning cases record real technical auto-repairs once
lessons.whenToUse: Validator/IRONCLAD automatically replaces or repairs an authored reference.
lessons.badPattern: Warnings say AUTO REPLACED while automaticCorrections remains empty, or duplicate validators record the same repair repeatedly.
lessons.goodPattern: Capture deduplicated issues plus technicalAutomaticCorrections so curation can distinguish authoring errors from successful fail-soft repairs.

lessons.title: Catalog, authoring, normalization, validation and runtime share one executable truth
lessons.whenToUse: Any rule that affects whether a Cutscene package is legal, repairable or renderable.
lessons.badPattern: Teach ChatGPT one rule, repair to a second shape, validate against a third rule, then let runtime silently interpret a fourth.
lessons.goodPattern: The exported contract is executable truth. A safe automatic repair either produces a canonical package that the same validator accepts and runtime interprets identically, or returns one clear blocker without leaving a half-repair.
lessons.lesson: Do not add a repair that creates a new validator failure. Preserve proven migration/binding/UI-duration/rollback fixes while deleting contradictory fallback folklore.

lessons.title: Generated Actor and Layer visibility is owner-bound and time deterministic
lessons.whenToUse: World actors and Layer actions that appear only in one sequence or shot.
lessons.badPattern: spawnWorldActor=true or a shot-local Layer Activate makes an object visible from time zero or lets it leak into later locations unless ChatGPT authors defensive cleanup everywhere.
lessons.goodPattern: Generated actors start hidden. A visible world action implicitly activates once for its sequence unless explicitly hidden; Enter/Activate explicitly show; Exit/Deactivate hide. Sequence-owned layers live for the sequence; shot-local layers live for their shot unless they refer to a sequence-owned layer.
lessons.lesson: Timeline state is derived from current time and owner interval, not callback history.

lessons.title: Temporary UI and VFX have deterministic before-inside-after state
lessons.whenToUse: ShowUi, generated UI, procedural effects and temporary VFX during playback or Timeline scrubbing.
lessons.badPattern: A radar, flash, vignette or effect stays visible after its clip or reappears depending on scrub direction.
lessons.goodPattern: Before interval hidden; inside interval visible/authored; after interval hidden. Activation tracks use inactive post-state and generated objects begin inactive.
lessons.lesson: Scrubbing backward, Evaluate(), rebuild and jumping into the middle must reconstruct the same state as forward playback.

lessons.title: Every VFX type has one explicit procedural-or-asset-backed policy
lessons.whenToUse: SpeedLines, Vignette, ScreenFlash, ColorFlash, Silhouette or Overlay.
lessons.badPattern: Attach a Ui-primary generated support sprite to an Effect field, or leave assetId empty and rely on an undocumented gray fallback.
lessons.goodPattern: SpeedLines, Vignette, ScreenFlash, ColorFlash, Silhouette and Overlay are canonical procedural built-ins and omit assetId. Other effect types require an exact Effect-primary asset or a visible diagnostic placeholder.
lessons.lesson: No hidden assetId="" -> gray sprite path, and no Ui-primary helper pretending to satisfy an Effect-primary destination.

lessons.title: Dialogue identity repair must end in a validator-valid presentation
lessons.whenToUse: A required speaker/listener portrait is incompatible with the Actor identity or unavailable.
lessons.badPattern: Remove the bad portrait, claim Preview is repaired, then leave FACE_TO_FACE_PORTRAITS or COMMAND_SCREEN requiring that now-missing visual.
lessons.goodPattern: Use exactly one visual source per participant. An explicit stage body wins and suppresses portrait fallback; when no body exists, try an exact same-identity compatible portrait, then use built-in participant fallback only when the selected preset explicitly exports allowsBuiltInParticipantFallback=true and the cast identity exists. Otherwise choose another exact compatible tuple/preset; if none is legal, return one clear blocker. Never silently downgrade to SUBTITLE_ONLY.
lessons.lesson: Normalizer and Validator are one contract, not rival departments. A repair is complete only when the canonical validator accepts it.

lessons.title: Editor evaluation never performs real audio playback
lessons.whenToUse: GenerateAtomic, PlayableDirector.Evaluate, Timeline scrubbing and deterministic Preview construction.
lessons.badPattern: ProcessFrame calls AudioSource.Play while the Director is only evaluating state, producing disabled AudioSource warnings and history-dependent sound.
lessons.goodPattern: Evaluation updates deterministic clip binding/time only. Real AudioSource.Play is allowed only during actual runtime Playback evaluation on an active enabled source.
lessons.lesson: Scrub/evaluate and playback are different execution modes. Do not suppress the warning; remove the invalid side effect.

lessons.title: Every generated visual must be traced before it is cosmetically fixed
lessons.whenToUse: Any unexplained square, overlay, actor, Layer, VFX or UI object appears in Editable Preview.
lessons.badPattern: Guess that an unexplained gray rectangle is Radar/Glow/Vignette and hard-code a workaround around the guess.
lessons.goodPattern: Trace generated debug metadata back to category, source action/event/entity ID, assetId, semantic type/preset and owner. Yellow unresolved placeholders remain explicit; unknown non-placeholder visuals are diagnosed before changing content.
lessons.lesson: Do not teach ChatGPT folklore from an unidentified visual artifact. First establish what generated it.

lessons.title: Readable story hierarchy comes before extra legal assets
lessons.whenToUse: Selecting layers, props, VFX and camera embellishment for an establishing, action or reveal shot.
lessons.badPattern: Stack many technically legal space images so a black-hole rescue reads as ships floating over one giant red blob.
lessons.goodPattern: Priority: recognizable location, focal actor, actor relationship, action direction, UI/dialogue readability, then restrained VFX/parallax/camera accents. Prefer fewer coherent elements.
lessons.lesson: Legal asset is not automatically useful storytelling asset. Use description/tags/review semantics for dramatic purpose, and simplify when uncertain.

lessons.title: Dialogue backgrounds contain zero baked runtime dialogue content
lessons.whenToUse: Choosing backgrounds, dialogue frames and communication-screen art.
lessons.badPattern: Use an attractive baked image that already contains a speaker name, sentence, portrait or fixed message, then overlay live dialogue on top.
lessons.goodPattern: Background = environment. Frame/container = blank reusable presentation. Speaker name, dialogue sentence, subtitle, runtime portrait and dynamic status content are rendered only by the runtime dialogue/UI system.
lessons.lesson: A visually attractive asset is structurally wrong when it bakes content the runtime owns. Prefer explicit annotation/manual review; do not build an OCR empire for this.

lessons.title: Learning evidence preserves stable issue occurrences and source contract identity
lessons.whenToUse: Capturing and exporting raw failure cases across contract revisions.
lessons.badPattern: Aggressive dedupe removes distinct Error occurrences, or an old failure is reviewed later without knowing which authoring contract produced it.
lessons.goodPattern: Dedupe by stable issue identity including code + jsonPath + entity/line identity + message (with narrow special handling for duplicate auto-replacement reports). Keep sourceContractRevision and classify Current, StillRelevantLesson or HistoricalFixed.
lessons.lesson: Two dialogue lines failing the same rule are two pieces of evidence. Old-contract failures stay evidence without masquerading as current regressions.

lessons.title: Distinct narrative people require distinct preferred Actor identities
lessons.whenToUse: Two or more named Person cast entries are authored.
lessons.badPattern: Pilot and Commander resolve to different frames of the same Actor family/preferred identity.
lessons.goodPattern: Resolve each distinct named person to a distinct Actor-primary preferred identity. Reuse the same identity only when intentionally representing the same narrative identity/clone.
lessons.lesson: Cast is identity. Animation/action frames do not manufacture new people.

lessons.title: Editable Preview build is disabled cleanly during Play Mode
lessons.whenToUse: The designer tries to rebuild while Unity is playing or changing Play Mode.
lessons.badPattern: Start generation, throw a build failure, and save it as if the JSON were bad.
lessons.goodPattern: Disable/refuse Build before generation with one concise state message; preserve the existing Cutscene and do not create a JSON learning failure.
lessons.lesson: Known Editor state is UX, not archaeological evidence.

lessons.title: Moving debris obeys Layer-vs-Actor placement truth
lessons.whenToUse: Rocks, meteorites, projectiles or scenery need visible movement.
lessons.badPattern: Put a Layer-only rock in cast[] merely because the story asks it to move.
lessons.goodPattern: Use Layer Move/Parallax for Layer-primary scenery/debris. Use Actor actions only with an Actor-primary movable object.
lessons.lesson: Movement does not override cutscenePrimaryUse.

lessons.title: Blockers first; routine fallbacks are Info or grouped notes
lessons.whenToUse: Validation produces blockers plus many review/fallback notes.
lessons.badPattern: Let repeated not-human-reviewed, missing voice, Neutral-expression or empty project story notes bury the real blocker.
lessons.goodPattern: Show REAL BLOCKERS first. Aggregate repeated review notes. Timed-text voice fallback, Neutral expression fallback, and empty project story idea when creativeIntent exists are Info-level guidance.
lessons.lesson: A designer should understand the one thing preventing Preview before seeing optional polish notes.

lessons.title: FACE_TO_FACE presentation is isolated per shot
lessons.whenToUse: A locked FACE_TO_FACE_PORTRAITS dialogue line is materialized.
lessons.badPattern: Globally forbid FACE_TO_FACE participants from cast entries with spawnWorldActor=true, or allow a world route to remain active during the portrait shot.
lessons.goodPattern: Use DialoguePortrait for portrait-only actors, WorldActor for world-only actors, and explicitly authored Both (for example {"role":"SupportingCharacter","displayName":"Commander","presentationMode":"Both","spawnWorldActor":true}) when world-action and portrait intervals are temporally isolated. Put world action before/after the locked dialogue shot; during FACE_TO_FACE use actorActions=[] and Hold or supported cut-based framing.
lessons.lesson: Locked FACE_TO_FACE requires portrait-only presentation during that shot. An actor may use an explicitly authored Both presentation in other world-action shots, but world and portrait representations must never overlap.

lessons.title: Directing intent compiles through a semantic firewall
lessons.whenToUse: Expressing shot purpose, camera intent, composition, motion, dialogue tone or dialogue pace in V3 authoring.
lessons.badPattern: Write semantic directing words directly into CURRENT shotType, cameraAction, actorAction or dialogue enum fields, or invent a value when CURRENT has no exact enum.
lessons.goodPattern: Author only the V3 semantic vocabulary; let the deterministic CURRENT compiler choose legal CURRENT values, record any fallback, and preserve sequence/shot/intent provenance.
lessons.lesson: Semantic intent describes what the audience should feel and see; the CURRENT compiler owns how that intent is serialized into the closed production contract.

goldenExamples.excerpt: DialoguePortrait or explicit Both with temporal isolation; FACE_TO_FACE_PORTRAITS uses actorActions=[] and a static Hold camera with legal speaker/listener portraits.

goldenPolicy: A full JSON enters GOLDEN only after real Unity LOAD -> NORMALIZE -> VALIDATE -> BUILD EDITABLE PREVIEW and a human visual check. The active book intentionally contains no full GOLDEN JSON until a candidate passes both the real build path and visual acceptance.

failedCasePolicy.capture: Validation failures and build failures are saved automatically into a local machine-only Learning Case Inbox. A built Preview that looks wrong is captured manually with SAVE VISUAL ISSUE.
failedCasePolicy.deduplication: Deduplicate only exact stable issue identities. Different jsonPath/entityId/lineId occurrences remain separate evidence even when the rule/code is the same.
failedCasePolicy.curation: Raw cases never modify the active Instruction Book automatically. Periodically export the inbox, classify each case, fix the correct subsystem, and distill only reusable lessons.
failedCasePolicy.promotion: A corrected full JSON becomes GOLDEN only after real Unity LOAD -> NORMALIZE -> VALIDATE -> BUILD EDITABLE PREVIEW plus visual acceptance.

rules.description: One serialized identity cannot ambiguously represent different Actors.
rules.defaultPolicy: Do not infer which Actor was intended.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Check all identity evidence before materialization.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No automatic repair.
rules.validationPolicy: Block ambiguous identity collisions.
rules.chatInstruction: Choose one canonical Actor identity explicitly.
rules.studioMessage: Actor identity collides with another canonical Actor.

rules.description: Actor visuals must resolve to the canonical Actor-primary identity.
rules.defaultPolicy: Animation frames and portraits are not identity defaults.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Resolve against current Catalog capability and identity evidence.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No automatic identity substitution.
rules.validationPolicy: Block unproven or conflicting Actor identity.
rules.chatInstruction: Use the Actor-primary canonical identity from CURRENT.
rules.studioMessage: Actor identity is not proven by this serialized value.

rules.description: Explicit animation IDs must belong to the selected Actor compatibility set.
rules.defaultPolicy: Only an underspecified semantic request may use a safe static fallback.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Resolve the exact serialized animation ID against CURRENT.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Never replace an explicit illegal animation with a guessed animation.
rules.validationPolicy: Block explicit incompatible animation IDs.
rules.chatInstruction: Use an animation ID listed as compatible for the Actor.
rules.studioMessage: Animation is not compatible with the selected Actor.

rules.description: Automatic Chat candidates are exact, materializable CURRENT assets with explicit Cutscene use; review-only fallback records are not suggested automatically.
rules.defaultPolicy: Manual/pinned assets remain user-owned, but automatic suggestions exclude unsafe, ambiguous and needsHumanReview records.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Project automatic Actor candidates to preferred canonical identity and include compatible same-identity dialogue portraits when available.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Do not auto-suggest generic fallback Layer records such as unclassified sprites merely because Preview can display them.
rules.validationPolicy: Explicit user-selected assets remain subject to normal destination validation.
rules.chatInstruction: Prefer suggestedCandidates for exact assets. Treat assets absent from the safe shortlist as deliberate choices that need stronger Catalog evidence.
rules.studioMessage: Automatic Chat candidate shortlist contains only exact CURRENT authoring-safe assets.

rules.description: Locked dialogue requires a deterministic stage background.
rules.defaultPolicy: The existing Dialogue Stage supplies the canonical background when omitted.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Do not substitute a Catalog visual.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No repair beyond the Dialogue Stage default.
rules.validationPolicy: Warn when omitted; continue only when the Dialogue Stage default resolves deterministically.
rules.chatInstruction: Use the canonical Dialogue Stage background default.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue Stage background default is required.

rules.description: Locked dialogue requires a deterministic dialogue frame.
rules.defaultPolicy: The existing Dialogue Stage supplies the canonical frame when omitted.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Do not substitute a UI or portrait asset.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No repair beyond the Dialogue Stage default.
rules.validationPolicy: Warn when omitted; continue only when the Dialogue Stage default resolves deterministically.
rules.chatInstruction: Use the canonical Dialogue Stage frame default.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue Stage frame is required.

rules.description: A multi-use Catalog asset is not ambiguous when the serialized destination already selects one legal use.
rules.defaultPolicy: A Layer field selects Layer use, an Effect field selects Effect use, and equivalent typed destinations select their own legal capability.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Validate the exact serialized asset against the destination; suppress generic multiple-use review noise when that destination is legal.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No asset substitution is performed.
rules.validationPolicy: Block only when the exact asset is illegal for the serialized destination.
rules.chatInstruction: Treat the JSON field destination as part of asset intent. Do not avoid a legal asset merely because Catalog also exposes another use.
rules.studioMessage: Typed destination resolved the Catalog multi-use ambiguity.

rules.description: Dialogue-only portraits cannot overlap an active world presentation without legal isolation.
rules.defaultPolicy: Do not infer Both from simultaneous references.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Validate presentation and temporal isolation before materialization.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No silent presentation fallback.
rules.validationPolicy: Block illegal world/portrait overlap.
rules.chatInstruction: Use dialogue-only presentation for FACE_TO_FACE_PORTRAITS.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue actor presentation conflicts with world staging.

rules.description: Dialogue presentation requires a deterministic background.
rules.defaultPolicy: The Dialogue Stage may supply its canonical background when omitted.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Do not invent a background asset.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No authoring fallback is allowed beyond the Dialogue Stage default.
rules.validationPolicy: Warn when omitted; continue only when the Dialogue Stage default resolves deterministically.
rules.chatInstruction: You may omit this field when using the canonical Dialogue Stage default.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue Stage default will supply the omitted presentation value.

rules.description: Dialogue font selection is project-owned when no explicit font is authored.
rules.defaultPolicy: Omitted fontAssetId uses the configured project TMP/RTL fallback.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply the shared project font fallback during materialization without emitting one validation issue per line.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No JSON repair is required for an omitted fontAssetId.
rules.validationPolicy: Block only an explicit invalid font requirement or an actual materialization failure, not omission itself.
rules.chatInstruction: Omit fontAssetId unless the scene deliberately requires a specific compatible font; project fallback is the normal default, including RTL text.
rules.studioMessage: Project dialogue font fallback applied.

rules.description: Optional reaction tail padding may not turn a valid final dialogue line into a blocker.
rules.defaultPolicy: Reaction timing belongs to the owning shot/sequence and its optional tail defaults to the remaining owner time.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Clamp negative/overflowing reaction offsets and holdAfterLine to the owning interval after dialogue duration is normalized.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Clamp mechanically and record the correction without changing the spoken line or Actor identity.
rules.validationPolicy: Explicit missing Actor identity or invalid owner timing remains a blocker.
rules.chatInstruction: Do not hand-tune reaction tails to fit the last frame; Unity clamps optional reaction padding to the owning interval.
rules.studioMessage: Reaction tail timing was fitted to its owner.

rules.description: Emotional Dialogue presentation is owned by the curated CharacterPack repertoire.
rules.defaultPolicy: Use only the exact published defaultExpression or an explicitly supported expression from the participant's authoring-ready CharacterPack; never derive or substitute a portrait.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply the closed-world repertoire gate before dialogue materialization.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Never borrow a portrait, promote a Catalog Actor, require a WorldActor, or fall back to Neutral for unsupported explicit intent.
rules.validationPolicy: Block when the exact curated CharacterPack identity or requested expression cannot resolve.
rules.chatInstruction: Author the exact Emotional Dialogue actorId and omit expressionIntent only when the CharacterPack default is intended.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue presentation was resolved from the exact curated CharacterPack.

rules.description: Fixed-layout Dialogue Stage mechanics are system-owned, while identity and expression remain closed-world CharacterPack data.
rules.defaultPolicy: Speaker/listener stage mechanics may default from the selected preset, but participant identity and presentation must resolve from EMOTIONAL_DIALOGUE_CURRENT.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply deterministic stage defaults only after the repertoire and exact expression have passed validation.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Never use stage defaults to promote an Actor, acquire a portrait, or repair an unsupported expression.
rules.validationPolicy: Block when no exact curated CharacterPack presentation route exists.
rules.chatInstruction: Author exact repertoire actorIds and supported expressions; omit only mechanical stage values owned by Unity.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue Stage mechanics defaulted after closed-world identity validation.

rules.description: Each dialogue participant has one primary visual source per presentation context.
rules.defaultPolicy: Portrait and body are not silently merged.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Validate visual source relationships after resolution.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No automatic source substitution.
rules.validationPolicy: Block portrait/body source conflicts.
rules.chatInstruction: Choose one visual source for each participant context.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue participant has conflicting visual sources.

rules.description: SUBTITLE_ONLY cannot acquire an unsupported portrait through fallback.
rules.defaultPolicy: Unsupported optional presentation is not repaired into another mode.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Validate preset capability against CURRENT.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No silent portrait fallback.
rules.validationPolicy: Block explicit unsupported portrait requests.
rules.chatInstruction: Use an explicit portrait-capable preset or keep subtitles only.
rules.studioMessage: Dialogue visual source is unsupported by the preset.

rules.description: Visible Effect obligations may occupy an optional sub-interval of their containing beat.
rules.defaultPolicy: Omitted startOffsetSeconds begins at beat start; omitted durationSeconds ends at beat end. Explicit duration is clamped to the beat end.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Resolve the interval once at the Simple -> existing V3/V5 execution-plan boundary, then pass that exact interval to the existing Effect materializer.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Do not apply these fields to Actors, Layers, Audio or other visible routes; do not deduplicate repeated Effect handles.
rules.validationPolicy: Block negative/non-finite offsets, non-positive/non-finite durations and starts at or after beat end. Overlap is legal.
rules.chatInstruction: Use startOffsetSeconds and durationSeconds only for visible Effect entries when a beat-local sub-interval is required.
rules.studioMessage: Effect sub-beat timing was resolved into the containing beat interval.

rules.description: Generated Cutscene output must not become authoritative Catalog input.
rules.defaultPolicy: Generated-root paths are excluded from Catalog source scans.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Validate the scan candidate boundary.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No repair after contamination; fail the consistency gate.
rules.validationPolicy: Block generated-root contamination.
rules.chatInstruction: Generated Cutscene output is runtime output, not authoring source.
rules.studioMessage: Authoritative Catalog scan includes generated Cutscene output.

rules.description: Generated entities belong to an explicit shot, sequence, location, or persistent owner.
rules.defaultPolicy: Default lifetime is the owning shot or sequence.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply ownership before materialization and cleanup planning.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No automatic persistence beyond the owner.
rules.validationPolicy: Block invalid location/lifetime leakage.
rules.chatInstruction: Declare persistence explicitly when an entity must outlive its owner.
rules.studioMessage: Generated entity ownership is invalid or leaks across owners.

rules.description: Mechanical IDs use deterministic owner namespacing.
rules.defaultPolicy: Generated IDs are deterministic from sequence/shot/entity context.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Normalize IDs before semantic validation.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Repair only when all references are unambiguous.
rules.validationPolicy: Block ambiguous duplicate references.
rules.chatInstruction: Let Unity generate mechanical IDs; do not invent identity IDs.
rules.studioMessage: Mechanical duplicate ID was deterministically repaired.

rules.description: Both requires explicit intent and legal temporal isolation.
rules.defaultPolicy: Legacy fields migrate only when the result is unambiguous.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Infer only a single deterministic presentation mode.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Do not infer Both.
rules.validationPolicy: Block ambiguous presentation mode.
rules.chatInstruction: Specify WorldActor, DialoguePortrait, or explicitly isolated Both.
rules.studioMessage: Presentation mode is ambiguous.

rules.description: Built-in procedural effects own their visual implementation and do not require an assetId.
rules.defaultPolicy: For an assetless procedural effect type, assetId is omitted.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Remove redundant assetId before validation when the effect type explicitly supports the assetless route.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Remove the redundant field without a yellow warning.
rules.validationPolicy: Block only illegal effect types or illegal explicit asset-backed routes.
rules.chatInstruction: For built-in procedural effects such as ScreenFlash, omit assetId unless the CURRENT contract explicitly requires an asset-backed effect.
rules.studioMessage: Procedural effect serialized in canonical assetless form.

rules.description: Locked portrait, monitor, and radio dialogue should author a held camera.
rules.defaultPolicy: camera.movement is hold or omitted for locked portrait/monitor/radio dialogue.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply at the Simple authoring boundary without rewriting explicit authored movement.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Do not auto-repair explicit movement; preserve the existing non-blocking diagnostic.
rules.validationPolicy: Warn when push, pull, follow, or track is authored on locked portrait/monitor/radio dialogue.
rules.chatInstruction: For locked portrait / monitor / radio dialogue, set camera.movement to hold or omit it. Put cinematic camera movement in an adjacent non-dialogue beat.
rules.studioMessage: Locked dialogue camera movement should be authored as Hold or omitted.

rules.description: Authoring fields must contain exact authoring IDs, not source/projection IDs.
rules.defaultPolicy: No default is safe for an explicitly serialized identity leak.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Inspect the serialized token before deserialization/materialization.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No automatic repair because identity meaning is ambiguous.
rules.validationPolicy: Block sourceRecordId, preview, catalog, and internal projection IDs in authoring fields.
rules.chatInstruction: Use the exact Catalog authoring ID.
rules.studioMessage: Serialized ID is not an authoring ID.

rules.description: A project-owned standardized 6x5 character sheet has one deterministic identity: portrait cells 0..11 and Body_Idle_Front cell 12 belong to the same source identity.
rules.defaultPolicy: Body_Idle_Front is the canonical Actor-primary world identity; Emotional Dialogue identity and portrait presentation remain owned by the curated CharacterPack.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Project this relation from the sheet contract during Catalog analysis and when rehydrating an older CURRENT snapshot.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Never promote arbitrary vendor sprite-sheet frames or unrelated characters into this identity contract.
rules.validationPolicy: Block only when an explicitly requested identity cannot resolve exactly; otherwise use the deterministic same-source relation.
rules.chatInstruction: For dialogue, use only the published CharacterPack actorId, identityHandle and supported expression; a standardized sheet is not a dialogue identity source.
rules.studioMessage: Standardized character sheet identity was projected deterministically.

rules.description: Unity owns baseline scale/proportion and background Cover framing.
rules.defaultPolicy: Authored scale defaults to 1.0; system-managed proportions apply where supported.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Normalize scale and background policy before visual QA.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Do not repair extreme explicit scale into a creative replacement.
rules.validationPolicy: Report extreme authored scale and visual framing separately.
rules.chatInstruction: Do not compensate for framing with arbitrary scale.
rules.studioMessage: System-managed scale/proportion/background policy applied.

rules.description: Optional authoring collections are deterministic empty collections.
rules.defaultPolicy: Missing optional collections default to [] where the Contract permits.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply before DTO deserialization and before semantic validation.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Add [] and record the correction.
rules.validationPolicy: Reject null only where the Contract requires a value.
rules.chatInstruction: Emit empty collections for optional fields.
rules.studioMessage: Optional fields default to empty collections.

rules.description: Locked dialogue without actor actions is dialogue-only.
rules.defaultPolicy: lockStaging=true with omitted actorActions defaults to [].
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply the empty collection before locked-dialogue validation.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Add [] and record an auto-repair.
rules.validationPolicy: Explicit actor movement/action remains invalid.
rules.chatInstruction: Do not author world movement inside locked dialogue.
rules.studioMessage: Locked dialogue actorActions defaulted to empty.

rules.description: Locked dialogue cannot contain explicit world movement/action.
rules.defaultPolicy: No default or fallback changes explicit creative movement intent.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Validate after defaults and before materialization.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: No automatic repair.
rules.validationPolicy: Block explicit movement/action in locked dialogue.
rules.chatInstruction: Use portrait staging and HOLD/cut camera framing.
rules.studioMessage: Locked dialogue contains explicit movement/action.

rules.description: CURRENT V5 bookkeeping fields with one deterministic value are system-owned defaults.
rules.defaultPolicy: When V5 is proven, omitted contextVersion and empty top-level mechanical collections use the CURRENT deterministic value.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Apply these defaults before canonical DTO validation; project/context binding remains owned by Studio.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Fill only unambiguous mechanical metadata. Never invent story, identity, duration, assets or creative intent.
rules.validationPolicy: Block contradictory version/identity evidence and genuinely missing creative data.
rules.chatInstruction: Start from the CURRENT canonical package shape, but do not spend creative effort on deterministic bookkeeping fields; Unity may fill them when omitted.
rules.studioMessage: Deterministic V5 envelope metadata was filled by the system.

rules.description: Extra fields outside the canonical V5 DTO are non-authoritative metadata and are removed at the import boundary.
rules.defaultPolicy: Unknown fields do not become part of the package contract merely because ChatGPT emitted them.
rules.normalizationPolicy: Prune unknown V5 properties before canonical field validation, then let required-field validation catch any real omission.
rules.autoRepairPolicy: Remove only fields that have no matching canonical public DTO field; never invent replacement story, identity or asset values.
rules.validationPolicy: Duplicate JSON properties, wrong types, missing required fields and invalid canonical values remain blockers.
rules.chatInstruction: Use only canonical V5 fields. Extra notes belong in supported extension valueJson, not ad-hoc properties.
rules.studioMessage: Unsupported non-canonical V5 field was removed by the import boundary.
